title: FORD TOWN FUN FEST 2026
full_story:
The location for the festival is in front of the Flora Public Library and Food trucks will be set up on East 2nd Street.

The event starts with a Cruise in tomorrow at 5 pm, starting at the parking lot of Beck’s Auto Sales with dash plaques to the first 100 entries.  The car show is open to any make or model of car.  They will be cruising through town and past Heritage Woods so the residents can look at the vehicles.  Food trucks inflatables and family yard games will be available at Library Park from 5 to 8 pm, and Just for Spite Unplugged will be playing from 6 to 9 pm.

Saturday the Clay County Cruisers will have a Car Show with registration from 9 until Noon.  The car show registration is $15 and there will be awards for the top 75 plus 5 specialty awards.  For Car show information call 618-676-4005, 618-662-5646 or 618-676-7732.  Dash plaques will be given to the first 100 entrants.  Craft and food vendors, inflatables, and games will also open at 9 am.  There are also commemorative T-shirts available for $20.

At noon the craft brew and chili cookoff sampling will begin and the dunking booth will open.  Car show awards are at 3 pm and craft beer and chili judging will begin at 4 pm.  So far there are 7 entries in the craft brew contest and 6 entries in the Chili Cookoff, with entries still being taken.  The winner of the Chili Cookoff will win a $100 gift card and have their name engraved on the Chili Cookoff Plaque in City Hall.  For more information call Arriel at the Chamber Office at 618-662-5646.

title: IECC BOARD
full_story:
The Board of Trustees of the Illinois Eastern Community College District met Tuesday evening at Lincoln Trail College, in Robinson.

A Public Hearing was held regarding the Fiscal Year 2027 Budget.  Following the hearing and having received no comments, the FY2027 Budget was approved as presented.  Approval was also given to authorize the Chancellor to file the FY27 Budget with the Illinois Community College Board in accordance with applicable requirements.

A $39,000 bid from Entec Services, Inc. of Mattoon was accepted for the Terry L. Bruce West Richland Center HVAC Unit Replacement project, with authorization for the administration to execute the necessary contract documents.

Andy Hill was approved for a change in status from FCC Bookstore Manager to District Campus Store Manager, effective September 21st.  The next regular meeting of the Board of Trustees will be on Tuesday, October 20th, at 6:15 pm at Olney Central College.

title: CLAY COUNTY TAX SALE
full_story:
Clay County, as Trustee, has completed their tax deed proceedings on real estate properties that were delinquent in 2022 and mobile homes that were delinquent for 2023 and prior real estate taxes.  The County, as Trustee, will now offer for sale the real estate and mobile homes obtained to the public through a sealed bid auction.

They will offer approximately 10 real estate items and 2 mobile home items through a sealed bid auction sale.  All sealed written bids must be in the Clay County Treasurer’s Office located in the Clay County Courthouse, at 111 Chestnut Street, in Louisville, no later than the close of business on October 2nd.  All online bids must be submitted via www. iltaxsalebids.com no later than the close of business on October 2nd.

The sale of these lots and mobile homes should be a major benefit to both the Taxing Districts and the neighboring property owners.  This sale will place the real estate and mobile homes into the hands of individuals who have an interest in owning them.  The County, as Trustee, hopes that these new owners will both maintain the property and the mobile homes and keep the taxes paid.  By eliminating abandoned properties, the appearance of the neighborhood should improve, and the value of adjoining properties should increase.

The required minimum bid on real estate is $844.00, and on mobile homes is $915.00.  All items will be sold to the highest sealed bid received on or before October 2nd.  Complete bidder’s packets and sale catalogs are now available at the Clay County Treasurer’s Office or online at www. iltaxsale.com.

For further sale information, contact the Auction Sale Department of the Clay County Tax Agent’s Office.  The telephone number is 1-800-248-2850 or 618-656-5744 or visit www.iltaxsale.com.  Office hours are 8:00 am and 5:00 pm Monday through Fridays.

title: EIU 10 DAY ENROLLMENT
full_story:
Eastern Illinois University’s Fall 2026 10th-day enrollment report reflects both the challenges and opportunities facing higher education today.  While overall enrollment stands at 7,651 students, the University’s newest class demonstrates continued academic strength, growing student success outcomes, and increasing interest in several high-demand academic programs.

Among the most promising indicators is the quality and persistence of EIU students.  Approximately one out of every five first-year students entered the University this fall with a perfect 4.0 GPA.  At the same time, EIU’s first-year retention rate increased nearly 2%, signaling continued progress in student success and persistence toward graduation.

Notably, EIU saw an 8% increase in enrolled students from within a 60-mile radius of EIU’s Charleston campus.

The University also welcomed its most significant proportion of first-generation students in more than a decade, with 53 percent of EIU’s incoming freshman class being the first in their families to attend college.  The milestone reflects EIU’s longstanding commitment to expanding educational opportunities and is aligned with the Illinois Board of Higher Education’s (IBHE) vision for a thriving Illinois.  EIU’s commitment to opportunity and access is further demonstrated through the University’s Panther First Generation Scholarship, which provides additional financial support to Illinois students with demonstrated need who are pioneering pathways to higher education for themselves and their families.

While the University saw significant gains in the new student academic profile and persistence year over year, overall enrollment declined as a result of fewer high school graduates, continuing international enrollment challenges, and a reduction in the college-going rate across Illinois as well as the nation over the past decade.  The impact of decreasing K-12 enrollments also contributed to fewer dual-credit enrollments.

The official 10th-day report remains the standard enrollment measure used by public universities throughout Illinois.

For more information about Eastern Illinois University, including its broad array of academic and career readiness programs, community-based services and opportunities, visit Eastern Illinois University or call EIU’s public information office at 217-581-7400.

title: CARLYLE LAKE TRIATHLON
full_story:
MSE Racing, in partnership with the US Army Corps of Engineers at Carlyle Lake Project and the City of Carlyle, will host the Carlyle Lake Triathlon on Sunday, September 20th.  The race begins at 7 am and includes sprint and Olympic distance options.

Athletes will start with a swim on the south side of Dam West Beach before transitioning to the bicycle course.  The bicycle route begins at the Main Dam and travels north along designated roads in Clinton and Bond counties.  The running portions will guide athletes through the West and East spillways, General Dean Recreation Area, Saddle Dam II and across the Main Dam to the finish line.

To ensure safety of both athletes and the public, the following areas will be temporarily closed:

Lake Road, from the West Spillway entrance to the Dam West Boat Ramp entrance on Saturday, September 19th at 9 am through Sunday, September 20th at 4 pm.  Saddle Dam II, from McNair Campground to the Dam East Boat Ramp entrance from Sunday, September 20th from 6 am until the conclusion of the race.

Several public areas will remain open during the event, though they will be actively used by the racecourse.  These areas include Dam West Day Use, the Main Dam, Clinton and Bond County roads, West and East Spillways and General Dean Recreation Area.

Visitors and residents are strongly encouraged to exercise caution when driving or recreating in these areas during the event.  Motorists should reduce speed near active race zones and follow all posted signs and instructions from event personnel.

Community groups or individuals interested in volunteering to assist with the event should visit the website: https://www.mseracing.com/carlyle-lake-triathlon.

For additional information, please contact the Carlyle Lake Project Office at 618-594-2484 or email [email protected].

title: US ATTORNEY WARN OF SPOOFING
full_story:
The US Attorney’s Office for the Central District of Illinois is alerting the public to recent reports of fraudulent phone calls in which scammers spoof official office telephone numbers in an attempt to deceive and defraud individuals.

These callers may claim to be employees of the US Attorney’s Office, use the names of real staff members, and pressure individuals with threats or demands for payment.  The US Attorney’s Office does not request money, personal financial information, or sensitive identifying details over the phone.

“The US Attorney’s Office remains steadfast in protecting the public and ensuring individuals are not exploited through impersonation schemes.  These scams succeed by casting doubt and fear into their victims, pressuring them to reveal information they would otherwise keep secure.  We will not allow these tactics to undermine the trust and safety of our communities,” said United States Attorney Gregory M. Gilmore.  “My office will never stop working to safeguard the citizens of the Central District of Illinois.”

If you receive a suspicious call, document the name and details the caller provides, hang up immediately and Call the US Attorney’s Office directly using the publicly listed numbers.  State that you may have been a target of a spoofing scam and ask to speak with the individual by name to verify whether the call was legitimate.

Anyone who believes they have been targeted by this scam is encouraged to report the incident to the FBI at https://www.fbi.gov/tips or 1-800-CALL-FBI (1-800-225-5324)

title: NEXT GENERATION OF MANUFACTURERS
full_story:
Governor JB Pritzker and the Illinois Department of Commerce and Economic Opportunity (DCEO) announced more than $20 million in capital grants to establish five new Manufacturing Training Academies (MTAs) at community colleges across downstate Illinois.  The academies will prepare Illinoisans for good-paying careers in advanced manufacturing while helping employers find the skilled workers they need to grow and create jobs.

The awards will support new and expanded training facilities at Illinois community colleges, including Illinois Central College, Kaskaskia College, Lake Land College, Lewis and Clark Community College, and Parkland College.  Programs will focus on high-demand fields, including automation, robotics, industrial maintenance, machining, metal fabrication, and biomanufacturing.

In our area Kaskaskia College in Centralia will get $6,000,000 for Automation, CNC Machining, Industrial Maintenance, Logistics, and Robotics.  And Lake Land College in Mattoon will get $3,000,000 for Automation, and Robotics.

The grants will fund construction, facility improvements, and modern equipment needed to prepare students for increasingly technical manufacturing careers.  The academies will also work with regional employers to align training with local workforce needs and connect graduates with available jobs.

title: MEDICAL CANNABIS EXPANSION
full_story:
Governor JB Pritzker and the Illinois Department of Financial and Professional Regulation (ID-FPR) issued medical cannabis dispensary licenses to 37 existing dispensaries which may now serve both adult use customers and medical patients at the same location.  Providing existing dispensaries with the ability to opt-in for a medical dispensary license greatly increases patient access across the state, while also eliminating unnecessary red tape for regulators and consumers alike.  This change also allows newer dispensaries issued under social equity lotteries the chance to serve medical patients, leveling the playing field for small businesses.

“Expanding access to medical cannabis is an important step toward ensuring Illinois patients have more op-tions to obtain the medicine they rely on,” said Mario Treto, Jr., Secretary of IDFPR.  “More dispensaries means better options and increased convenience for medical patients, while still maintaining the regulatory safeguards that protect patients and promote a safe and responsible cannabis industry.”

Under the new law, an adult-use dispensary with an active license in good standing may apply for a medical cannabis dispensary license.  Once approved by IDFPR, the dispensary may sell cannabis to registered medical cannabis patients at the medical tax rate, up to the patient’s authorized allotment.

“This is a monumental day for medical patients, who have long advocated for these changes,” said Erin A. Johnson, Cannabis Regulation Oversight Officer.  “We are also proud to expand opportunities for the many small cannabis businesses who have wanted to serve medical patients for years.”

A list of these new medical licenses is available on IDFPR’s Adult Use Cannabis webpage.  Additional medical cannabis dispensary licenses are expected to be issued on a continuing basis.  This means that any new dispensary opening in the State of Illinois will have the option to seek a medical cannabis dispensary license and serve patients.

“IDFPR has been advocating for expanded access to the medical cannabis market, and this change creates meaningful opportunities for both patients and dispensaries,” said Vaughn G. Bentley, Deputy Director of the Cannabis Control Section at IDFPR.  “We are committed to implementing SB 3222 in a way that expands access while ensuring dispensaries understand and comply with all applicable requirements.”

This is the biggest expansion of the medical cannabis market in Illinois since 2016.  The medical opt-in provision is one of several changes to Illinois’ cannabis laws enacted through SB 3222, which Governor Pritzker signed into law on June 12th.  The legislation also made changes related to dispensary operations, licensing, possession limits, medical cannabis, and other aspects of Illinois’ cannabis regulatory framework.

“Expanding the number of dispensaries able to serve medical cannabis patients is good policy for Illinois,” said state Rep. Bob Morgan.  “It means patients have greater access and more choices, while dispensaries have new opportunities to grow their businesses and better serve their communities.  This is an important step toward building a stronger, more accessible medical cannabis program in Illinois.”

There are currently 288 adult use cannabis dispensaries in Illinois, including 178 dispensaries from social equity lotteries that have opened their doors.  There are 68 conditional licensees from social equity lotteries in the process of working toward their full dispensary licenses. IDFPR will continue to issue full adult-use dispensary licenses and medical dispensary licenses as applicants continue to seek to open both their adult use, and now medical, dispensaries.
